- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4feccc26851b89dcb8f4d78dfab011e73d12c128` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `673f24a38292b2920d60fc28684761d5952c9512` — the merge of head `d8dc243c15cf9d4ab12b5905d3f66b3f70a47c26` into base `4feccc26851b89dcb8f4d78dfab011e73d12c128`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 673f24a38292b2920d60fc28684761d5952c9512 && git checkout 673f24a38292b2920d60fc28684761d5952c9512
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4feccc26851b89dcb8f4d78dfab011e73d12c128 d8dc243c15cf9d4ab12b5905d3f66b3f70a47c26 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4feccc26851b89dcb8f4d78dfab011e73d12c128 && git merge --no-ff d8dc243c15cf9d4ab12b5905d3f66b3f70a47c26

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4feccc26851b89dcb8f4d78dfab011e73d12c128
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4feccc26851b89dcb8f4d78dfab011e73d12c128` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d8dc243c15cf9d4ab12b5905d3f66b3f70a47c26`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/controlled-by-parent-every-row-master.test.ts, .changeset/25049-cbp-every-row-master.md + packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts, packages/core/src/utils/required-emptiness.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/errors.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md

Face: `narrowing`. `reviewFace` on the three changed paths decides no face and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line; `hits` is empty, so the Scope floor is every path of the diff and the rest is cited code. Read against `main` at the merge base `a39389eb51` (the head is that base merged into `1b27f979b4`): three files, +616/−8, all inside `@objectstack/plugin-security` plus one changeset. No governed path, no `packages/spec/**`, no `packages/objectql/**`, and `computeControlledByParentFilter` is untouched — the claim's file-surface fence held. ⛔ The disclosure ruling recorded on #9387 (`5323310017`) applies to this record: reach is stated abstractly and no shape is named for any path this PR leaves open.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Verdicts, never a scope** (ruling record `6303721609`, letter B) — RIGHT. Both new questions end in a throw (`PermissionDeniedError` from the one walk, or `MasterReferenceMissingError`) or a return; nothing is written onto `opCtx.data`, `opCtx.options.where` or `opCtx.ast`. No master set is composed into any write and no second spelling of a master scope appears anywhere in the diff.

2. **One walk, once per master, in row order, before anything is written; nothing written on refusal** — RIGHT. The batch loop (`security-plugin.ts` 9314–9333) calls `assertControlledByParentChainEditable`, the same extraction every other shape calls, and `assertMasterRowEditable` stays the single leg set — once per distinct master (`asked.includes`), rows iterated in order, the first refusal propagating. It runs inside the security middleware, which `ObjectQL.insert` invokes through `executeWithMiddleware` ahead of the executor that writes (`engine.ts` 7034–7075, 15901–15940); `insertMany` is `insert` with `__partialRowErrors` (17117–17120), so one chain pass covers it too and a middleware throw never reaches the executor. The protocol's `createManyData` and `insertManyData` call exactly those two engine methods (`protocol.ts` 17080–17190). On a delegated write both principals' passes precede the executor. Pinned: refusal-envelope equality with the single create and `null` storage for every row across four doors on five leg × caller cases; the order pins `asked: [f2, f1]` and `asked: [f1, h]`.

3. **The batch then meets the empty-master branch exactly as before** (seat ruling B on the PR's question 2, `6312332660`) — RIGHT. Line 9334 is unchanged: `masterId` stays `undefined` for an array, so the branch at 9368 answers as it did — stands down for `insert` under `omissionRefusedByValidation`, else `422` whole. The one ordering consequence is that the walk is asked first, so under an unjudged declaration a batch naming a master the caller may not edit now answers `403` where it answered `422` — still a refusal, nothing admitted. The agent-pass-first consequence is declared in the acceptance notes and pinned.

4. **The emptied-reference rule** — RIGHT on each point the brief asks, with one residual carried in ③.
   - Hand-over exactly where validation provably judges the same field: `omissionRefusedByValidation` is `master_detail` + `required` + not `readonly` + not `system` (8565). `validateRecord`'s update branch (`record-validator.ts` 1989–2015) walks `Object.entries(data)`, reaches a field only when `isInReadonlyScope` admits it (686–689: a `system` field never, a `readonly` field shape-only), and refuses `def.required && isEmptyForRequired(def, value)` as `required_cleared`. The mirror is exact for the required-cleared check, and the predicate is not widened (the freeze note's bar).
   - Asked after the stored masters' question: by-id at 9489 then 9494; predicate at 9353 then 9360. Pinned (stored-master-first `403` on all three shapes).
   - All three update shapes: `extractSingleId` (7545) reads a scalar body `id` or a scalar `where.id`; every other shape `resolveEngineUpdateDispatch` calls `multi` takes the predicate path. Pinned on all three, for three callers, with the leave-it-out control landing. A predicate update that selects no readable row is not asked and writes nothing, consistent with the write doors' narrowing.
   - Own-property `undefined` read as empty: RIGHT. `Object.entries` enumerates an own key whose value is `undefined`, and `isMissing(undefined)` is true (`required-emptiness.ts` 51–53), so validation refuses it on a judged declaration exactly as the gate refuses it on an unjudged one.
   - The acceptance note on the engine's update strip ("where before the key was dropped … fails closed") is accurate, read against `rule-validator.ts`. _[Seat redaction, under the #9387 ruling: one clause naming which declaration the engine strips is held privately.]_

5. **Changeset headline and bullets** — the headline and every Now / Unchanged bullet claim nothing the diff does not make true; each is pinned or read in code (the import door's `writeBatch` throws on a refused batch and the runner degrades to per-row `createData`, `import-runner.ts` 1032–1075, 1083, 1232). The two Before bullets describe the defect at its upper bound: "landed whatever masters" held only under the judged declaration (an unjudged one was already refused whole), and "landed and stored the null" held only for one of the unjudged declarations. Neither over-states the accept set now shipped; both over-state what landed before. Not a correction this record demands.

6. **Docblocks** — the `[#25044]` sentence is now true of the batch create; the `#7474` list, the `#8688` paragraph, the freeze note and the chain-walk docblock each gained the matching sentence, and the freeze note's "do not widen `omissionRefusedByValidation`" is honoured.

7. **Test file** — 18 cases on a real stack (`ObjectQL` over better-sqlite3, the real `SecurityPlugin`, sharing service and protocol, contexts from `resolveAuthzContext` / `assembleExecutionContext`); it reads nothing outside its package; `Test Core` ran it on this head.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/plugin-security: minor` with a `!` title and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body, the changeset and both amended claims (`6312286163`, `6312297497`) — RIGHT. Nothing is admitted that was refused before, and two shapes that landed are refused: a narrowing no conversion carries. Under the amended 「甲」 (`6303865025`, rule 2) that ships now as a BREAKING minor in the changeset shape the amendment names, which this changeset mirrors (BREAKING paragraph, Before / Now / Unchanged, What to do). No other package publishes from this diff. `Check Changeset` is green.
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — RIGHT: no spec key, authorable spelling, stored shape or export moves; the "What to do" is a grant or a kept-populated reference, not a rewrite of consumer code; `Lint & Repo Gates`, which carries the registration gate, is green on this head.
- Full dogfood battery on the final head (the os-dev rule for a `!` / narrowing PR): recorded in the report's `dogfood_battery` field and in the PR body for `d8dc243c15` — 286 files passed, 3 skipped; 2387 tests passed, 18 skipped; no shard, no path; lock verdict exit 0. Recorded as the rule requires; this review re-ran nothing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR open question 1 (does this PR close #25068 too) — answered A (`6312332660`): row 6 of the door table is that card's whole reading and its pins are in this PR (three callers × three update shapes plus the validation and stored-master-first controls). Both `Fixes` lines are right; `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` and `Part-of PR must not also close its card` are green.
- Open question 2 (answer a batch row by row under an unjudged declaration) — answered B, kept as shipped; the seat declined the loosening and left it to a maintainer's word. Consistent with ①3.
- Open question 3 (a defect outside the write gate) — filed abstractly as #25092 (`6312332660`); outside this PR's change and not re-derived here.
- Acceptance notes (whole-call refusal on `insertMany`; `403` ahead of validation's `400` for a master with no row behind it, as a single create already answers; agent-pass-first; the body read before the engine's strips) — each a declared fail-closed consequence, none widening.
- One further shape, in the emptied-reference rule's reading of "empty" — held out under the disclosure ruling; escalated to the seat privately with its topology and remedy options. It is a pre-existing property of the walk this PR reuses, not a regression, and it admits nothing this gate refused before.
- Check-runs on `d8dc243c15cf9d4ab12b5905d3f66b3f70a47c26`: every concluded run `success` except seven `skipped`, all on `check-expected-skips.mjs`'s roster (the two opt-in harnesses; the full-battery-only `Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Dogfood Verify CLI` and the dogfood shard template; `Build Docs`).

**VERDICT: PASS**
